notes: §1985:X.2.4.1 (4): in a program's initial state 'A GO TO statement referred to by an ALTER statement contained in the same program is set to its initial state.' AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitFields declares each alterable GO TO's target as an INSTANCE field initialized to the written target, EmitAlter assigns it and EmitGoTo dispatches on it, so the initial state is whatever a new program instance holds: ProgramTable.CancelNode drops the instance (and those of contained programs, reverse order) so the next CALL builds a fresh one, and an INITIAL program gets a fresh instance per call; ALTER itself is refused only from 2002 (COBOL0810 at 2023). Probed at 85: a non-initial callee with two GO TOs altered by one ALTER kept both altered across CALLs and found both reset after CANCEL; a contained program's sectioned altered GO TO reset when its container was cancelled and when its INITIAL container was called again; ALTERs written under IF that change the GO TO target between calls followed the latest ALTER; the witness calls an INITIAL program twice and sees the unaltered GO TO each time.

next.reason: 1985: "A GO TO statement referred to by an ALTER statement contained in the same program is set to its initial state."; 2023: "Initial-state list (14.6.2.3.2) covers fill, VALUE data, file connectors, screen items, based items, tables, lengths; no GO TO/ALTER". The 2023 initial-state rules list every action taken and none resets altered GO TO statements; the ALTER feature this rule served is absent from the 2023 texts.
